title: He didn’t fall asleep in sin.
paragraphs: He didn’t fall asleep in sin.
Meet Eutychus—the young man almost nobody preaches about in Acts 20.

Sitting in a window.
Listening to Paul the Apostle preach.
Let that sit for a second.

Not rebellion.
Not scandal.
Not secret sin.

The danger wasn’t the window.
It was the drift.

The kind of drift that happens when truth becomes familiar…
and fire turns into background noise.
Some scholars interpret this as a warning against spiritual dullness—not that sleep itself is sin, but that a disengaged heart can become vulnerable even in sacred spaces.

You can be in the room…
and still fall.

You can hear the Word…
and still miss the voice of God.
Paul the Apostle doesn’t preach a sermon about discipline.
Wraps himself around the lifeless boy.

Not because you hated God…
but because you drifted.
And now it feels like something in you has died.
But Jesus doesn’t stand at the window shaking His head.
And through the cross and resurrection of Christ—

what was dead
can live again.
This isn’t just a story about falling.
It’s a story about being carried back up.

If your fire feels gone…
if your heart feels heavy…
if you’ve been drifting more than fighting—
Because grace still runs toward falling people.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
